name: TemplateSensor
description: Template sensor profile. Copy this and customize for your sensor.
guide:
Quick Start Guide
==================

- Resolution: configurable via SIZE field in .cfg
- I2C: see I2C_ADDR and I2C_MODE in .cfg
- For detailed register map, see the sensor datasheet

Register Groups
---------------
- Exposure / framing: integration time, frame rate control
- Window / readout: ROI (region of interest) settings
- ADC / gains: analog and digital gain controls
- MIPI / CSI-2: data link configuration
- Power / state: sensor state machine

Notes
-----
- Always write LSB before MSB for multi-byte registers
- Some registers require the sensor to be in standby mode
- Use the GUI's Sensor regs tab for interactive register editing

tabs.preview: Live video preview from the sensor. Use Controls tab to adjust exposure and gain.
tabs.controls: Dynamic controls loaded from the .cfg file (e.g., Exposure, Gain, Framerate).
tabs.registers: Register-by-register editor. Pick a register to see its description and bit-level details.
tabs.advanced: USB transfer tuning, sensor mode selection, SDK log level.
tabs.info: Sensor identification, firmware version, and SDK debug messages.

registers.name: Sensor state
registers.help:
Controls the main state machine.

0 = Standby (analog blocks idle, registers accessible)
1 = Streaming (MIPI active, frames produced)

Use this to stop/start capture without losing register values.

registers.name: Exposure time (rows)
registers.desc: EXP_TIME (16-bit) — integration time in row periods
registers.help:
Exposure duration expressed as a number of row scan periods.

T_exposure[s] = EXP_TIME × ROW_LENGTH / CLK_IN

Write LSB (addr 0x0202) before MSB (addr 0x0203).

registers.name: Frame length (rows)
registers.help:
Sets the vertical frame period (in rows).

T_frame[s] = FRAME_LENGTH × ROW_LENGTH / CLK_IN

Increasing FRAME_LENGTH reduces the framerate without touching exposure.

registers.name: Window width
registers.help: Number of pixels to read per line. Set to full width or less for windowed mode.

registers.name: Window height
registers.help: Number of rows to read. Full height or less for windowed mode.

registers.name: Analog gain
registers.help:
Pre-ADC gain control. The exact gain multiplier depends on the sensor.
Typically 100 = 1x, 200 = 2x, etc. (consult datasheet).

Higher values increase sensitivity at the cost of dynamic range.

registers.name: Digital gain
registers.help:
Applied after the ADC. Fixed-point format: 1.0x = 0x100 = 256.

Example: 0x200 = 2.0x, 0x80 = 0.5x

Less noise than analog gain at the cost of reduced SNR.

registers.name: Lane count
registers.desc: Number of active D-PHY data lanes
registers.help:
Configures how many parallel MIPI data lanes are used.

0 = 1 lane (lower bandwidth, reduced resolution or fps)
1 = 2 lanes (standard)
2 = 4 lanes (high bandwidth)

Must match host receiver configuration.

registers.name: Bit depth
registers.help:
Selects the ADC output resolution.

8-bit:  highest speed, lowest SNR
10-bit: balanced
12-bit: typical for RAW sensors
14-bit: maximum dynamic range (if supported)

Lower bit depths free MIPI bandwidth and allow higher framerates.

registers.name: Chip ID
registers.help: Unique hardware identifier burned into the sensor. Use this to verify the sensor type.

registers.name: Frame counter
registers.help: Increments once per output frame. Useful for detecting dropped frames.
